title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. G is GL_2 or SL_2 over a base, and every object is a section or a group scheme. The page continues §VIII, which recapitulates §III on the 'équation des lacets' (1): [α,ρ] = [β,σ] ε_1(ν).
- ρ and σ are fixed regular sections of G.
- T_ρ and T_σ are their stabilizers, i.e. centralizers, which are tori in the regular semisimple case.
- ε_1: G_a → L_1 ⊂ G parametrizes a unipotent subgroup L_1 that enters the equation itself.
- B'_0 is a 'pré-Borel'. In a suitable basis it is the affine ('ax+b', mirabolic-type) group {[[μ,λ],[0,1]]}.

The proposal (previous page) is to parametrize solutions (α,β,ν) by the map
(2) B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ → G_{ρ,σ}, (u,a,b) ↦ (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, ν(u)),
for a suitable morphism ν: B'_0 → G_a. Writing ρ(u) = ρuρ^{-1}, the map lands in the solution scheme iff identically
(3) ρ(u) = ε_1(-ν(u)) σ(u).
So ρ(u) and σ(u) must agree modulo L_1 for every u in B'_0.

This page analyses when that holds.
- Necessity. Grothendieck argues that it is hard to imagine unless L_1 ⊂ ρ(B'_0) =: B'_1. Then (3) forces σ(B'_0) ⊂ B'_1, hence equality, by the 'known argument': both are smooth connected 2-dimensional subgroups, or one argues via conjugacy of such subgroups. It also forces L_1 = (B'_1)_u, the unipotent radical.
- Sufficiency. Conversely, suppose ρ(B'_0) = σ(B'_0). Equivalently σ^{-1}ρ normalizes B'_0. The normalizer of the affine group in GL_2 is the Borel B_0 of upper triangular matrices, so this means σ^{-1}ρ is a section of B_0. Then σ(u) and ρ(u) are two sections of B'_1 with the same determinant, namely det u. Since B'_1/(B'_1)_u ≅ G_m via det, they coincide modulo (B'_1)_u = L_1. This defines ν(u), given that ε_1: G_a ≅ L_1.
- Conclusion. The key condition for getting solutions via (2) is (σ^{-1}ρ)(B'_0) = B'_0, i.e. σ^{-1}ρ ∈ Γ(B_0).

Uniqueness. Next comes uniqueness of the representation (α,β,ν) = (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, ν(u)).
- The fibres of (2) carry the action (u,a,b) ↦ (ut, at, bt) for t in T_ρ ∩ T_σ ∩ B'_0 (stated on the next page).
- So injectivity requires (5): T_σ ∩ T_ρ ∩ B'_0 = {1}.
- The insertion justifies this: for instance, T_ρ ∩ T_σ should be the centre (G_m), and G_m ∩ B'_0 = {1}.

Margin NB. The condition σ^{-1}ρ ∈ B_0 apparently says, geometrically, that ρ and σ carry the flag (line) fixed by B_0 to the same flag, i.e. the same Borel.

Next page. Surjectivity is reduced to surjectivity of u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ],ν(u)) onto the scheme H_{ρ,σ}. Grothendieck then questions whether the 'draconian' hypotheses of §II are really needed.

Purpose. The page serves to give an explicit, scheme-theoretic, group-parametrized description of the solution scheme of a GL_2/SL_2 commutator ('loop') equation. This is presumably a local building block in Grothendieck's study of the Teichmüller/Galois tower in rank 2.
errors: The necessity of L_1 ⊂ ρ(B'_0) is only heuristically argued ('se conçoit difficilement si on n'admet pas'), not proved.

The step from σ(B'_0) ⊂ B'_1 to σ(B'_0) = B'_1 uses an unspecified 'argument connu'. It holds over a field, or for smooth connected group schemes with connected fibres of equal dimension. Over a general base it needs flatness or connectedness hypotheses.

Identifying 'σ^{-1}ρ normalizes B'_0' with 'σ^{-1}ρ is a section of B_0' is correct in GL_2: the normalizer of the affine group is the Borel. Over a general base the normalizer should be taken scheme-theoretically.

The relation between condition (5) and the marginal condition (T_ρ∩T_σ central, G_m∩B'_0 = {1}) is only sketched. The text says 'il faut si possible', so (5) is not shown to be sufficient for injectivity.

ideas.what: Parametrizing solutions of a commutator equation [α,ρ]=[β,σ]ε_1(ν) in GL_2 by the orbit-type map B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ → solution scheme.
ideas.modern_name: Explicit parametrization of a fibre of a representation/character scheme of a surface-type relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: General character-variety literature (Fricke, Goldman, etc.); this specific construction unknown

ideas.what: The normalizer of the affine (mirabolic-type) 'pré-Borel' subgroup is the Borel. Two such subgroups conjugate by ρ and σ coincide iff σ^{-1}ρ lies in the Borel.
ideas.modern_name: Normalizer of the mirabolic/affine subgroup; Bruhat-type position of Borels
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 contains the general normalizer/Borel theory

ideas.what: Two elements of B'_1 with the same determinant agree modulo the unipotent radical, since B'_1/(B'_1)_u ≅ G_m via det.
ideas.modern_name: Levi quotient of a solvable group
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (general structure of solvable/Borel group schemes)

ideas.what: Injectivity of the parametrization modulo the free action of T_ρ ∩ T_σ ∩ B'_0, with condition (5) that this intersection is trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Stabilizer/freeness condition for an orbit parametrization

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates σ^{-1}ρ ∈ B_0 (ρ and σ send B'_0 to the same pre-Borel) as the essential condition for a group-parametrized solution family of the GL_2 loop equation. On the next page he openly asks whether the stronger 'draconian' hypotheses of §II are needed for surjectivity. This sharpened parametrization question appears never to have been settled in print.
missed.quote: Ainsi on voit que la propriété essentielle pour obtenir des solutions de (1) via (2), c'est d'avoir (σ^{-1}ρ)(B'_0) = B'_0 i.e. σ^{-1}ρ ∈ Γ B_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would give explicit rational parametrizations of components of SL_2/GL_2 character schemes of punctured-surface relations over arbitrary bases. That is of mild interest for arithmetic character varieties and Galois actions on them, but likely recoverable by specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but elementary algebraic-group analysis: normalizers, unipotent radicals, freeness of a stabilizer action. It belongs to an unpublished computational project, and the ideas themselves are standard.
transcription_corrections: 'qui ont = déterminant - zéro [?] alors' is likely 'qui ont même déterminant – à savoir dét(u) –' (same determinant).
'[unicité]' is probably preceded by 'Pour l'unicité de la représentation d'un (α,β,ν)'. The third component should read ν (as in (2)), not γ.
In the inserted condition, 'T_ρ ∩ T_σ fixe' probably reads 'T_ρ ∩ T_σ = G_m' (centre), with 'G_m ∩ B'_0 = {1}', not 'G_u ∩ B'_0'.
'multiplication {+à g+} par' is probably 'multiplication à gauche par' (left multiplication by L_1).
'un peu modéré L_1' is likely 'un paramétré L_1' (the parametrized unipotent subgroup L_1).
